sammendrag: The Jobseeker’s Allowance (JSA) literacy and numeracy pilots were established in September 2001 to examine the use of sanctions and incentives to encourage jobseekers in the UK to take part in basic skills assessments and training. The pilots also investigated the ‘optimum timing’ of screening and the type of screening tool being used. The evaluation of the pilots involved two waves of interviews with clients who had been assessed by a jobcentre as having a basic skills need. The second wave followed up clients four to five months after the first interview. Key measures used to evaluate the effectiveness of the pilots were attendance at independent assessment, training starts and completions, qualifications and employment outcomes. The evaluation found that the presence of sanctions and incentives had a positive impact on independent assessment attendance rates. In relation to training, incentives areas performed better than sanction areas in terms of getting people to start training. Five per cent of respondents had achieved a qualification and respondents who had completed basic skills training were more likely to be employed at wave two than they were at wave one. Over 50% of respondents thought that it was likely that they would participate in training or education within the next two years.
tittel: Evaluation of JSA literacy and numeracy pilots: final report
